<section class="article-section">

        <h2>Tangent Hyperplanes: Local Linear Structure in Nonlinear Dynamics</h2>
        <p style="margin-bottom: 2rem; font-size: 1.1rem; line-height: 1.8; color: var(--text-dark);">
          This series explains what tangent-space linearization does and does not justify. Nonlinear flows
          generally do <em>not</em> superpose over finite time, but their first-order variations are linear
          at a specified state, trajectory, and contact mode. The articles below distinguish infinitesimal
          exactness from finite-step approximation and make the residual terms explicit.
        </p>

        <!-- Canonical series — tangent-hyperplanes-series/ -->

              Part I &mdash; Geometry

            <a href="../articles/tangent-hyperplanes-series/part-2-dynamics.html">
              Part II &mdash; Dynamics
            </a>

          <p>Derives the variational equation along a nonlinear trajectory and explains why superposition applies to the linearized perturbation model, not to the full nonlinear flow.</p>
        </div>

        <div class="article-card">

            <a href="../articles/tangent-hyperplanes-series/part-3-control.html">

              Part IV &mdash; Residuals and Curvature
            </a>
          </h3>
          <p>Shows how second-order residuals arise from nonlinear curvature and how those residuals bound the useful range of a tangent approximation.</p>
        </div>
